page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 120.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 1.88 GB per vCPU, positioning the instance specifically for compute-intensive workloads that do not require large memory footprints.

This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These design choices optimize the instance for pure CPU processing power, reducing overhead costs associated with unused local storage or accelerator hardware.

The c4d-highcpu-64 is qualitatively cost-efficient for high-density CPU tasks due to its dedicated resource allocation and streamlined hardware profile. It is suited for workloads such as batch processing, distributed compute jobs, web serving, and CI/CD pipelines. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for large-scale database hosting or deep learning training, but highly effective for parallelized CPU-bound applications.
